entry.title: Day 40 of 100 days dsa coding challenge
entry.summary:
Taking on a new challenge: solving GeeksforGeeks POTD daily and sharing my solutions! 💻🔥 Problem:
https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/problems/shortest-common-supersequence0322/1 Shortest Common Supersequence Difficulty: Medium Accuracy: 55.62% Given two strings s1 and s2, find the length of the smallest string which has both s1 and s2 as its sub-sequences. Examples: Input: s1 = "geek", s2 = "ek" Solution: dp = [[0] * (m + 1) for _ in range(n + 1)]
for i in range(1, n + 1): for j in range(1, m + 1): if s1[i - 1] == s2[j - 1]: dp[i][j] = 1 + dp[i - 1][j - 1] else: dp[i][j] = max(dp[i - 1][j], dp[i][j - 1])
lcs_length = dp[n][m]
scs_length = n + m - lcs_length
return scs_length
